results.name: Kettlebell Single Arm Chest Fly
instructions: Lie on a flat bench with your feet firmly on the floor and hold a kettlebell above your chest using a neutral grip.
Keep a slight bend in your elbow and slowly lower the kettlebell out to the side in a wide arc.
Lower until you feel a comfortable stretch across your chest while keeping your shoulders supported on the bench.
Bring the kettlebell back above your chest along the same path, then repeat before switching sides.
tips: Keep your shoulders and upper back firmly against the bench.
Lower only as far as your shoulder remains comfortable.
Keep your chest up and your torso still during each repetition.
Inhale as you lower the kettlebell and exhale as you raise it.
results.description: Kettlebell Single Arm Chest Fly is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with a kettlebell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Biceps, Forearms.

results.name: Kneeling Push-Up
instructions: Kneel on the floor and place your hands slightly wider than shoulder-width.
Walk your hands forward until your body forms a straight line from head to knees.
Lower your chest toward the floor by bending your elbows.
Press back up and repeat.
tips: Keep your hips in line with your body.
A good step toward full push-ups.
results.description: Kneeling Push-Up is a beginner multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Triceps, Front Shoulders, Core.

results.name: Landmine Chest Press
instructions: Begin by standing with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding the end of a barbell with the right hand at chest level. The other end of the barbell should be anchored securely in a landmine attachment or corner.
Press the barbell forward and slightly upward until your arm is fully extended.
Squeeze your chest muscles at the top of the movement.
Slowly lower the barbell back to the starting position at chest level. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your back straight and avoid arching it during the press.
Exhale as you press the barbell forward and inhale as you lower it back.
Focus on using your chest muscles to press the barbell.
results.description: Landmine Chest Press is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with a barbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Triceps, Core.

results.name: Lying Pull Over With Resistance Band Cable
instructions: Attach the middle of the resistance band to a low anchor point behind you. Lie on your back on the floor, knees bent and feet flat on the floor, holding a handle in each hand with your arms extended straight above your head, palms facing forward.
Keeping your arms straight, pull the handles over your head and towards the floor until your arms are in line with your body.
Slowly return the handles to the starting position with control, keeping your arms straight.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Exhale as you pull the handles over your head and inhale as you return them to the starting position.
Maintain a slight bend in your elbows to reduce strain on your joints.
Focus on engaging your lats and chest muscles throughout the movement.
results.description: Lying Pull Over With Resistance Band Cable is a beginner multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the lats (back). Performed with a band, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Triceps.

results.name: Machine Chest Press Decline
instructions: Sit on the decline chest press machine with your feet flat on the floor. Grasp the handles with both hands at chest level, palms facing down.
Press the handles forward by extending your arms, keeping your elbows slightly bent at the end of the movement.
Squeeze your chest muscles at the bottom of the movement and slowly return the handles to the starting position with control, bringing them back to chest level.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your back pressed against the backrest throughout the exercise.
Focus on engaging your chest muscles throughout the movement.
Exhale as you press the handles forward and downward, and inhale as you return them to the starting position.
results.description: Machine Chest Press Decline is a beginner multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with a leverage machine, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Triceps.

results.name: Machine Chest Press Incline
instructions: Sit on the incline chest press machine with your feet flat on the floor. Grasp the handles with both hands, elbows facing the floor, palms facing forward.
Press the handles upward by extending your arms, keeping your elbows slightly bent at the end of the movement.
Squeeze your chest muscles at the top of the movement and slowly return the handles to the starting position with control, bringing them back to chest level.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your back pressed against the backrest throughout the exercise.
Focus on engaging your chest muscles throughout the movement.
Exhale as you press the handles forward and downward, and inhale as you return them to the starting position.
results.description: Machine Chest Press Incline is a beginner multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with a leverage machine, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Triceps.

results.name: Machine Fly
instructions: Sit on the chest fly machine with your feet flat on the floor and your back pressed firmly against the backrest. Grasp the handles, arms parallel to the floor, with both hands at chest level and palms facing forward.
Keep a slight bend in your elbows and your arms extended out to your sides.
Bring the handles together in front of your chest by squeezing your chest muscles, keeping your elbows slightly bent.
Slowly return the handles to the starting position with control, bringing them back to your sides. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your back pressed against the backrest throughout the exercise to maintain proper form.
Focus on engaging your chest muscles throughout the movement.
Exhale as you bring the handles together and inhale as you return them to the starting position.
results.description: Machine Fly is a beginner single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with a leverage machine, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Biceps.

results.name: Normal Push-Up
instructions: Begin in a plank position with your hands placed slightly wider than shoulder-width apart and your feet together. Your body should form a straight line from head to heels.
Engage your chest and lower your body towards the floor by bending your elbows, keeping them at a 45-degree angle to your body.
Lower your chest until it is just above the floor.
Push through your hands to raise your body back to the starting position, fully extending your arms. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your elbows at a 45-degree angle to your body to maximize chest and triceps engagement and reduce shoulder strain.
Breathe steadily, exhaling as you push up and inhaling as you lower yourself.
Keep your head aligned with your spine to avoid straining your neck.
results.description: Normal Push-Up is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Triceps.

results.name: One Arm Push Up
instructions: Start in a push-up position with your feet wide and one hand under your chest.
Place your other hand behind your back.
Lower your chest toward the floor, keeping your body straight.
Press back up and repeat, then switch arms.
tips: Widen your feet for balance.
Start with your hand on a raised surface.
results.description: One Arm Push Up is an advanced multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Core, Obliques.

results.name: Pec Deck Fly Machine Flies
instructions: Adjust the seat so the handles are at chest height and sit with your back flat against the pad.
Grip the handles or place your forearms on the pads, arms open to the sides.
Bring the handles together in front of your chest.
Return slowly to the open position and repeat.
tips: Keep a slight bend in your elbows.
Don't let the weight stack slam between reps.
results.description: Pec Deck Fly Machine Flies is a beginner single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with a leverage machine, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Front Shoulders.
